2609.21392.title: Omni Demand Understanding: A Benchmark for Contextual User-Intent Inference in Multimodal Interaction
2609.21392.paper_summary: Natural audio-visual interaction is emerging as an important interface for AI assistants, allowing users to communicate through speech and vision rather than carefully composed text prompts. However, existing benchmarks of interactive capabilities still focus primarily on response quality, leaving a more fundamental question underexplored: can a model correctly infer the user's underlying demand from complex multimodal interaction? Real-world user demands are often underspecified in speech and must be inferred from multimodal cues and dialogue history. This inference is further complicated by ambiguous or disfluent expression and noisy acoustic environments. Conversely, request-like speech may not constitute a demand to the assistant, leading to false triggers. We establish Omni Demand Understanding (ODU) as a distinct multimodal contextual inference problem: given an interaction stream, a model must detect whether a user demand is present and infer intent from multimodal and conversational context. ODU evaluates this capability along five dimensions, covering both single-turn and multi-turn interactions. We construct ODU-Bench using a challenge-driven taxonomy, taxonomy-guided agentic video generation, and human-recorded interactions, followed by media-grounded annotation and human verification. We evaluate 14 native MLLMs. Even the strongest, Gemini 3.1 Pro, recovers only 44.7% of key information that must be inferred from visual, acoustic, or conversational context. Moreover, 11 of the 14 models exhibit false-trigger rates above 50% on non-demand scenarios. These results reveal a systematic capability gap in current MLLMs' ability to infer contextual user demands. We hope ODU can establish the evaluation of a previously underexplored yet essential capability in multimodal interaction: correctly understanding user demands before generating an appropriate response.
2609.21392.paper_summary_zh: 自然音視互動正逐漸成為 AI 助手的重要介面，使用戶能夠通過語音和視覺進行交流，而不是仔細編寫的文本提示。<lb/>然而，現有的互動能力基準仍然主要集中在回應質量上，留下了一個更根本的問題未被深入探討：模型能否正確推斷用戶潛在的需求，從複雜的多模態互動中？<lb/>現實世界中的用戶需求往往在語音中表達不夠明確，必須從多模態線索和對話歷史中推斷出來。<lb/>這一推斷因為模糊或不流暢的表達以及嘈雜的聲學環境而變得更加複雜。<lb/>相反，類似請求的語音可能不構成對助手的需求，導致錯誤觸發。<lb/>我們將 Omni Demand Understanding (ODU) 確立為一個獨特的多模態上下文推斷問題：給定一個互動流，模型必須檢測用戶需求是否存在，並從多模態和對話上下文中推斷意圖。<lb/>ODU 沿著五個維度評估這一能力，涵蓋單輪和多輪互動。<lb/>我們使用挑戰驅動的分類法、分類法引導的主動視頻生成和人類錄製的互動來構建 ODU-Bench，隨後進行媒體基礎的標註和人工驗證。<lb/>我們評估了 14 種本地 MLLMs。<lb/>即使是最強的 Gemini 3.1 Pro，也僅能從視覺、聲學或對話上下文中恢復 44.7% 的關鍵信息。<lb/>此外，14 種模型中有 11 種在非需求場景中顯示出超過 50% 的錯誤觸發率。<lb/>這些結果揭示了當前 MLLMs 在推斷上下文用戶需求方面的系統性能力差距。<lb/>我們希望 ODU 能夠建立對多模態互動中一個先前未被深入探討但至關重要的能力的評估：在生成適當回應之前，正確理解用戶需求。
